title: Choose the visual world
question: The roll assigned The Bench Notebook. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll. All four are light, cool-neutral, single-azure, and can only show state the server actually returned.

options.label: The Bench Notebook
options.lineage: a researcher's bench notebook with printouts taped in
options.thesis: The thread is a notebook page, and every agent output is a printout you taped in, dated and initialled.
options.viewport: Left rail of tabbed agents, a ruled thread down the middle, and dated evidence slips pinned to the right edge of the message you are reading.
options.risk: Paper metaphor turns decorative if the evidence slips ever hold a number the server did not return.

raised.raise: Evidence slips are hairline-ruled modules with their own caption tab and tile edge-to-edge, with none of the whitespace inflation of a default SaaS card grid.
A printed key at the foot of the rail defines every state symbol once, and the streaming layer rides above the record without ever rewriting it.
Each slip carries a monospace provenance line: provider, model, latency, estimated tokens, hierarchy by type scale alone rather than by shadows.

options.label: The Shift Log
options.lineage: a written shift-handover book, one ruled entry per action
options.thesis: Every entry is timestamped, attributed to who did it, and carries its own state; a blank line means nothing happened.
options.viewport: One continuous log down the page; the agent you are talking to is the current entry, and older agents are earlier pages in the rail.
options.risk: This is where most agent products land, an activity feed with a chat box; it works, and it will not look distinctive.

options.label: The Dense Tiled Record
options.thesis: Say more per screen with hairline-ruled modules and zero wasted pixel.
options.viewport: A tight mosaic of ruled modules, each headed by a small azure tab naming its agent and state.
options.case: Wins on audience identification for a technical operator who wants density; loses on clarity because a mosaic scatters the one thing that must stay linear, what happened in order.
options.risk: Small type on a light ground fails contrast fast, and multi-module density buries the thread.
options.kept: The hairline module system, caption tabs, and density courage.

options.label: Fixed Notation, Live Overlay
options.lineage: orienteering map and its ISO legend
options.thesis: Colour is a fixed truth table defined once in a legend, and a live route layer rides above without editing the ground.
options.viewport: The record sits on a fixed colour language; the streaming reply is a single azure route drawn over it, never repainting the record.
options.case: Fuses strongly on clarity, since notation that cannot lie is this product's whole claim; loses narrowly on identification because nobody carries a topographic map in their head at work.
options.risk: Its native palette is multi-hue, which breaks your single-accent rule the moment the legend grows past three symbols.
options.kept: The legend as a contract, and the rule that the live layer never rewrites the record.

options.label: The Parameter Readout
options.thesis: Near-white paper, ink black, one accent, and hierarchy built from type scale alone with no ornament at all.
options.viewport: One enormous statement of what the agent just did, with a small monospace block beneath listing exactly which model produced it.
options.case: The monospace parameter readout is the single best idea in the hand for honest evidence; as a whole world it is about letterforms, not about the operator's task.
options.risk: Scale-contrast-only hierarchy collapses on dense operational screens where nothing is the headline.
options.kept: The provenance readout, and hierarchy by scale rather than by boxes and shadows.

options.label: The Nixie Counter
options.thesis: Counts are the interface, and a number changing is a visible physical event.
options.viewport: Banks of glowing digits for calls, tokens and runs, labels engraved in caps beneath.
options.case: Declined on both axes: a dark chassis with orange glow contradicts your pinned light single-azure palette, and glowing digits read as instrumentation theatre where the product needs a record.
options.kept: A count change animates as a transition, so a number never teleports.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.lineage: the screenshot you pasted, built properly
canonCard.thesis: Conversation rail, message bubbles, evidence cards, composer with attach and mic, at full craft.
canonCard.viewport: Exactly the arrangement you showed me, executed impeccably, with our real data in the cards.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every other agent product, which is precisely what you asked for.
